world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

tone_statements.citation: Mouton, Léa. 2023. Esquisse grammaticale du hmong noir : étude comparative de l'expression de l'espace dans les langues hmong [A sketch grammar of Black Hmong: a comparative study of the expression of space in Hmong languages]. Thèse de doctorat (Sciences du langage), Université Lumière Lyon 2, dir. Alice Vittrant. 387 pp. NNT 2023LYO20072; HAL tel-04457297.
tone_statements.quote: Cette section s’attache à décrire le système tonal de la variété de hmong noir étudiée. La langue présente un système relativement riche de 7 tons lexicaux. Chaque syllabe est réalisée avec un ton. ... Pour résumer, le système tonal du hmong noir est composé de sept tons isolés comprenant des tons ponctuels et des tons complexes. - La présence de tons ponctuels se justifie par l’opposition de trois hauteurs de la voix. Les tons extra-haut, moyen et bas sont contrastifs. ... Le type de phonation est également contrastif au sein des tons complexes. Le ton moyen descendant murmuré contraste avec le ton moyen descendant craqué.
tone_statements.translation: This section describes the tone system of the Black Hmong variety under study. The language has a relatively rich system of 7 lexical tones. Every syllable is realised with a tone. ... To sum up, the tone system of Black Hmong consists of seven isolation tones comprising level tones and complex (contour) tones. - The level tones are justified by an opposition of three pitch heights: the extra-high, mid and low tones are contrastive. ... Phonation type is also contrastive within the complex tones: the breathy mid-falling tone contrasts with the creaky mid-falling tone.
tone_statements.locator: p. 100 (§4.4 Système tonal) and p. 104 (§4.4.3 Synthèse); inventory Tableau 23 p. 101, comparison Tableau 24 p. 104, sandhi §4.4.4.1 pp. 105-108
tone_statements.summary: 7 tones: 55, 33, 22, 41, 325~25, 32 breathy, 31 creaky; TBU syllable; sandhi 41/31 -> 32̤ after 41; morphotonemic -m~-d alternation.

tone_statements.citation: Mouton, Léa. 2022. Première étape dans le travail de description du hmong noir (Vietnam) : évaluation de la vitalité de la langue. Moussons : recherches en sciences humaines sur l'Asie du Sud-Est 40: 175-189. doi:10.4000/moussons.10066 (HAL hal-04609975).
tone_statements.quote: les consonnes finales graphiques marquent les tons de la langue (<-b, -j, -ø, -v, -g, -s, -m, -d>) – le nombre de tons dépend des variétés. Le mot hmong, par exemple, s’orthographie de la façon suivante : <hmoob>. Ici la consonne graphique <b> ne transcrit pas un phonème, mais note un ton haut égal (Mouton, 2018).
tone_statements.translation: the written final consonants mark the tones of the language (<-b, -j, -ø, -v, -g, -s, -m, -d>) - the number of tones depends on the variety. The word hmong, for example, is spelled <hmoob>. Here the letter <b> does not transcribe a phoneme but marks a high level tone (Mouton 2018).
tone_statements.locator: article pp. 175-189; paragraph on the RPA orthography
tone_statements.summary: Tonal; RPA tone letters; -b = high level in Black Hmong.

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien Language History. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics, ANU. Open access, ANU Open Research hdl 1885/146760
sources.note: Comparative, family-level only; does not mention Hmong Don. p. 11: 'All Hmong-Mien languages are tonal, and the primary function of tone is lexical discrimination.' The only stress remark (p. 28) concerns Mienic: quoting Downer 1961:539 on Mien reduced syllables having 'weaker stress and shorter duration than the following full syllables so that a strong iambic rhythm is imparted to disyllabic words'. Nothing on word stress in Hmongic.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 16th ed. Dallas: SIL. Entry 'Hmong Don' (hmf), web version archived 2010
sources.note: 'Comments: Tonal, 7 tones.' Region 'Ha Giang Province, Hua Binh, YenBai, Nghia Lo'; classification Hmong-Mien, Hmongic, Chuanqiandian; no population estimate. No stress statement. (Current ethnologue.com entry could not be reached by automated download.)

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Hmong language' and Wikipedia (vi) 'Tiếng H'Mông', 'Người H'Mông'
sources.note: Tertiary. en: Hmong Don (hmf) and Hmong Dô (hmv) are Vietnamese varieties 'not very well classified', 'very poorly known', no population estimates; no stress discussion. vi 'Người H'Mông': Vietnamese subgroups Hmông Trắng (Hmoob Dawb/Đơưz), Hmông Hoa, Hmông Đỏ (Hmoob Lees), Hmông Đen (Hmoob Dub/Đuz), Hmông Xanh, Na Miểu; Yên Bái mainly Hmông Hoa and Hmông Đỏ; no references given for the classification.

sources.note: A full contrastive phonology of Vietnamese and Hmong (tones, initials, rimes); the most complete modern phonology of Hmong in Vietnam found. Whether it treats the Hmong Đen/Đu variety (hmf) or Hmong Lềnh/Trắng must be checked; likely to state whether Hmong has word stress. Full text held in the National Library of Vietnam thesis database (login required).
